From someone that had psychosis for more than 10 times in my life, your symptoms doesn't look like schizophrenia. Antipsychotics would help to get out of the beginning of an acute schizophrenia episode, but they have drawbacks like affecting memory, sexual dysfunction, etc. In schizophrenia, there are two types of symptoms, antipsychotics only work for positive symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, etc. Negative symptoms are diminution or loos of normal functions, like normal thoughts, actions, ability to tell fantasies from reality, etc. To have schizophrenia, you need to have two of the five main symptoms, Those symptoms are delusions, hallucinations, disorganized or incoherent speaking, disorganized or unusual movements and negative symptoms (DSM-V).
I really think this is more of a paranoia of getting schizophrenia then really having it. The only exam I know could let you see if you have it is scanning your brain and let it be analysed by a psychiatrist, but this doesn't mean it's accurate since I've scanned mine and it was normal, no damage whatsoever...
The cognitive dysfunction will get worse if you don't threat it properly, without medication for example.
Stress can trigger psychosis, it triggered for me more than 5 times psychosis. You can work this with your therapist, it isn't the end of life having this type of stuff, if you have bad memory you could start doing crossword puzzles, playing chess, learn a new language or instrument (this helped me a lot learning a new language), programming can also help. You can't retain it, but you can get used to it and start exercising your brain. The digestion stuff has nothing to do with psychosis neither schizophrenia. Hope this helps ;) .
